previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a man with a history of acute on chronic systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, ischemic cardiomyopathy, type 2 diabetes, and chronic kidney disease, was admitted for chest pressure and worsening shortness of breath due to fluid overload. Despite reporting adherence to medications, recent emotional stress and dietary factors contributed to the exacerbation. He initially resisted IV diuresis due to concerns about side effects, leading to a prolonged course with fluctuating treatment adherence. His condition improved with a combination of IV and oral diuretics, and adjustments to heart failure medications, though his kidney function worsened slightly. He elected to discontinue IV therapy and was discharged home on oral torsemide with close follow-up in the heart failure clinic. His chest pain resolved with diuresis and was not due to acute coronary syndrome.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic (congestive) heart failure
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease with stage 1 through stage 4 chronic kidney disease, or unspecified chronic kidney disease
Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery without angina pectoris
Presence of coronary angioplasty implant and graft

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ with sCHF (EF 30% ___ w/ multiple 
admissions, 2 vessel CAD w/ DES to LCx, h/o VT and afib s/p ICD, 
DM2, htn/hl who presented hypervolemic with acute on chronic CHF 
exacerbation. 

#Systolic CHF, acute on chronic exacerbation: Patient appeared 
grossly hypervolemic on admission with a 2L O2 requirement. 
Patient was initially diuresed with large doses of Lasix 160mg 
IV boluses, plus Lasix drip at 20mg/hr with limited urine 
output. Was given metolazone which greatly increased diuresis 
but cause a mild ___. After a two day diuretic holiday, diuresis 
was restarted and the patient's symptoms resolved. Patient's 
home diuretic dose was decreased to torsemide 140mg qd from 
160mg as he was a bit negative on that dose. 

# CAD - History of two-vessel coronary artery disease, LCx 
totally occluded and RCA with a distal 60% lesion, s/p PCI of 
LCx with drug eluting stents. Pt reported chronic upper 
epigastric pain on admission which was unchanged from baseline. 
No acute changes on EKG on arrival. Troponin mildly elevated 
most likely d/t CKD, with flat CKMB. Continued on aspirin. 
Plavix was discontinued as he is more than one year out from his 
last drug eluting stent and is on aspirin and warfarin.

history of atrial fibrillation and VTach s/p ICD. ICD 
interrogation showed several short runs of atrial tachycardia 
and no VT. Patient was started on warfarin at ___ while

discharge and should be monitored.
